title: Creme Brulee
subtitle: Baked vanilla custard with a thin caramel crust
excerpt: The French custard with the crack. A rich baked cream infused with vanilla and finished with a thin layer of burnt sugar. Simple and very satisfying to make.
sourceNotes: Classic French dessert with roots in 17th-century French court cooking.

recipe.batchNotes: Makes up to 8 easily in the same water bath.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Custards can be made and chilled up to 2 days ahead. Brulee the sugar just before serving.

content.text: This makes 4 individual creme brulees and takes about 1 hour including cooking, plus 3 hours chilling. The critical thing to watch is the oven temperature: the custards need to be just barely set with a slight wobble in the centre when you take them out. They firm up perfectly as they chill.
Use only the egg yolks here, not the whole egg. Whites make the custard rubbery and tight. Six yolks is the correct ratio for this quantity of cream.

items.prepNote: plus 4 tsp for the brulee topping

content.text: Heat oven to 150C. Put 4 ramekins into a deep baking tin.
Heat the cream with the vanilla pod and seeds in a small saucepan until it just starts to steam. Do not boil it.
Whisk egg yolks and 80g sugar together in a bowl until pale and combined. Do not whisk in too much air.
Pour the hot cream slowly into the egg mixture, stirring constantly. Strain through a fine sieve to remove the vanilla pod.
Divide the custard between the 4 ramekins. Pour boiling water into the baking tin to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Remove ramekins, cool, then chill for at least 3 hours.
To serve, sprinkle 1 teaspoon of caster sugar evenly over each custard. Use a kitchen blowtorch to caramelise the sugar until amber and cracked. Serve within 5 minutes.

items.symptom: Custard is grainy or has bubbles across the surface
items.cause: Cream added too hot or too fast to the eggs, scrambling them
items.fix: Pour hot cream in a very thin stream, stirring constantly, and always strain before baking

items.symptom: Custard still liquid in the centre after 40 minutes
items.cause: Oven too cool or water bath not hot enough
items.fix: Extend by 10 minutes, ensuring the water was boiling when added

items.symptom: Caramel topping is sticky and will not crack
items.cause: Humidity in the air or sugar layer too thick
items.fix: Use a finer, more even sugar layer and brulee immediately before serving, not ahead of time

content.text: Creme brulee has been served at grand French tables since the 17th century. The name simply means burnt cream. It appears in cookbooks from both France and England from the 1600s, and both countries claim credit for inventing it. The French version, enriched with cream and finished with a thin caramel shell, became the definitive form and is found on the menu of every serious French restaurant worldwide.
